hafod_ranger.text: Diolch! The lease is yours? Then you'll want to know, the farm's been Enclosure Ltd's for years and the farmer's family is long gone to the town.
I'm the farmer they've kept on. I'll show you round, and I'll try not to say 'in my day'.

then.text: Closely grazed, drained, sprayed and fenced, and it still doesn't pay. Nobody's ever fixed that by doing more of the same.
Fewer sheep, trees going in along the becks. The neighbours think I've gone soft. The neighbours may be right. It looks lovely, though.
Hawthorn's coming up in the ffridd and the curlew's back on the rushy pasture. My father'd say I've lost my mind. Then he'd go and look.

else.text: Kites over the cwm every morning. A farm and a nature reserve in the same field, and the books balance. Just. Tell nobody.

hafod_shepherd.text: Every ewe knows her own bit of mountain. I don't know how, nobody does. I just know she'll go back to it if I drive her off the other side. Faster than the quad bike, too.
Wet again. It's always wet. I'd complain but I'd run out of day.
